because the findings were foundations-level and page-level fixes applied

whose findings drove the fixes; recording five rounds of one view would make
the gate arithmetic meaningless. All six reviewers of round 5 read ONE frozen
capture, sha256

applied AFTER the round and the tree re-exported and re-captured, which is what a
resolution IS. Each one names the source change, and several carry a measurement
taken on the rebuilt page. Rounds 1-4 are not recorded; recording five rounds of
What the loop measured, rather than asserted:
round 1  6/6 reviewers led with the same P1 — the product's entire call to
action rendered as the weakest control on the page. The primary
button measured 1.04:1 before and 6.29:1 after.
round 2  that P1 is gone from all six. New: the section-heading level
collides with the hero identifier; one grey does four jobs.
round 3  L2 measures the rhythm and reports 'one scale, correct proximity',
and that 'the classic label/value misalignment this view is warned
about did not happen'. L1 calls the type scale 'sound'.
round 4  the last foundations P1 clears. Remaining findings are P2/P3.
round 5  RECORDED BELOW. ZERO P1s carry a rubric criterion — every P1 is a
presence failure. L3 independently measured every text-on-surface
pair and reported no contrast failures anywhere.
Every round-5 P1 is a PRESENCE failure — age, a copy affordance, the value /
nonce / type rows, the receipt payload, the 'supply an ABI' action. That is
content nobody has built. All fifteen are recorded verbatim, none is
resolved, and the FULL gate holds every one against this page (G1 and G3 both
fail). They are VD.4's. The foundations gate excludes them by construction —
a finding with no rubric criterion is a missing element, and a missing
element is content — and prints the whole excluded set on every run rather
than dropping it.

G4 and G5 are EMPTY and stay empty. Both require a named human — brief §11
says so of G5 in as many words ('Not an agent'), and gate.mjs enforces `by`
and `date` on both. No agent may create them. Writing a plausible name into
either field would be the one edit that defeats the gate, so the foundations
round reports FAILED on exactly those two conditions and on nothing else.
That is the honest ceiling of an agent-run round, and it is where VD.2 stops.

missing: Hero: copy affordance on the full hash

findings.location: hero, between the H1 hash line and the trace card
findings.finding: The hero carries only the truncated hash, a 'Succeeded' pill and the full hash string. Age is absent from the page entirely, the finality badge appears only as a 'Pending' row inside the Overview grid rather than in the hero, and the full hash at y approx 288 has no copy affordance of any kind.

findings.location: Overview grid, rows BLOCK through COST · MANA
findings.finding: The grid has six rows: BLOCK, CANONICAL, FINALITY, FEE PAYER, TARGET, COST · MANA. Value, nonce and transaction type are absent as labelled rows, and COST · MANA is a resource limit/usage pair, not the required fee breakdown, so no fee figure appears anywhere on the page.

findings.location: Decoded input section, note box below the SELECTOR / RAW table
findings.finding: The unknown-selector path shows raw bytes plus the sentence 'Supplying an ABI decodes them.' set as ordinary body prose. There is no 'supply an ABI' action - no button, no link, no distinguishing type treatment - so the required affordance is present only as a description of one.

findings.location: hero, H1 hash line and the full-hash line 30px below it
findings.finding: The H1 truncates the hash to 10+8 characters at ~32px, and the complete 66-character hash is then set immediately beneath it at ~14px. The visually dominant instance is the incomplete one and the truncation buys nothing. The breadcrumb above truncates the same hash again at 6+4, so one identifier appears at three different lengths inside 130 vertical pixels with no single truncation rule.

findings.location: hero, 'Succeeded' badge to the right of the H1
findings.finding: The status badge is the smallest type in the hero at roughly 11px, set beside a ~32px H1. Status is the second most important fact on a transaction page and on a product whose reason to exist is reverted transactions; at this weight the hierarchy says the hash matters and the outcome is an annotation.

findings.location: Overview grid, COST · MANA value cell
findings.finding: '42000 / 100000 mana(FeeJuice)' sets the two figures, the unit and the token name at one monospace size, weight and colour, so the unit reads as more identifier. The digits carry no thousands grouping, and there is no space before '(FeeJuice)'. The unit and token should drop to the secondary text level so the numbers are the scannable part.

findings.location: hero, full-hash line at y approx 288
findings.finding: The full hash is set at the same size, weight, colour and face as a value cell in the Overview grid and carries no label. Typographically it reads as an orphaned table value that lost its row rather than as the page's canonical identifier.

findings.location: H1 versus the six section headings (Overview, Decoded input, Events, Internal calls, State changes, Raw (chain-native))
findings.finding: The H1 is monospace while every section heading is the proportional sans. The page's top heading level therefore does not sit on the same scale as its second level, and the six section headings are the only true heading rung the eye can navigate by.

findings.location: Raw (chain-native) section, JSON block
findings.finding: The JSON is set at roughly 13px on a ~1.55 line-height, barely denser than the 14px body around it. This is the one product-register element on a web-register page and the density difference should look chosen; at present it reads as the same rhythm on a grey surface.

findings.location: 'Raw (chain-native)' section heading
findings.finding: The parenthetical qualifier is set at the same size and weight as the heading noun, so 'chain-native' competes with 'Raw' for the scanning eye. Every other section heading is a single word or short phrase, making this one visually the longest and heaviest.

missing: Hero: copy affordance on the full hash
Decoded input: 'supply an ABI' action for the unknown selector

findings.location: hero, y163-296 (breadcrumb to full hash line)
findings.finding: The hero shows status ('Succeeded' badge at x843-1015) and the full hash (y284, x505-904) but omits three required items: the age, the finality badge, and any copy affordance beside the full hash. Finality is present only as a 'Pending' row inside the Overview grid at y874-915, which is not the hero.

findings.location: Overview grid (y791-1039), Decoded input note (y1325-1402), Raw block (y2351-2522)
findings.finding: Required data is absent. The Overview grid has only six rows (Block, Canonical, Finality, Fee payer, Target, Cost · Mana) - no value, no nonce, no transaction type, no fee breakdown. Decoded input states 'Supplying an ABI decodes them' as prose with no action control. The Raw block contains a single 5-line transaction object and no receipt payload, and the two payloads are not labelled or distinguished.

findings.location: all six section headings (Overview y742, Decoded input y1169, Events y1534, Internal calls y1790, State changes y2046, Raw y2301)
findings.finding: Every section heading is equidistant between the divider above it and the content below it: rule-to-heading is 28-30px and heading-to-content is 25-30px at all six sections (e.g. rule y712 -> 'Overview' y742 = 29px; heading bottom y760 -> table top y791 = 30px). No heading is bound by proximity to the block it labels, so across eight sections in one scroll the page reads as an evenly spaced strip of rules and items rather than six titled sections.

findings.location: right edge of the content column, whole page
findings.finding: Two container widths alternate down the right edge. Section rules, the Overview table, the Decoded-input table and the Raw block all end at x=1415 (911px wide); the trace card and all four notice boxes end at x=1203 (699px wide). The step repeats five times, and inside a single section - Decoded input - the table ending at 1415 sits 23px above a note ending at 1203, a 212px jog within one section.

findings.location: section aprons, y1503-2171 (Events, Internal calls, State changes)
findings.finding: The spacing apron is identical regardless of what the section holds: 100-101px above each rule, ~29px rule-to-heading, ~28px heading-to-content, for a 249px Overview table and for a 76-77px one-sentence notice alike. Events, Internal calls and State changes therefore consume 668px of vertical scroll to deliver three single sentences. The amount of space is not readable as a decision.

findings.location: trace card, hairline divider at y544
findings.finding: The divider inside the trace card runs x529-1138 while the card's content box runs x529-1178 (border 504-1203, padding 25px, confirmed by the Generate trace button's left edge at x529). It is inset 25px on the left and 65px on the right, so the only rule inside the page's most prominent card is visibly asymmetric.

findings.location: Overview table (x504-1415) and Decoded-input table (x504-1415)
findings.finding: Both tables are stretched to the column rather than sized to their data. The Overview table's longest value ends at x=1042, leaving a 373px dead column to the right of every row; the Decoded-input table's longest value ends at x=772, leaving 643px. At 1920 this is the wide viewport being consumed rather than used.

findings.location: boundary between the trace card (bottom border y620) and the first section rule (y712)
findings.finding: That gap is 92px, where every other section boundary measures 100-101px (y1039->1139, y1402->1503, y1658->1759, y1915->2016, y2171->2272). The one boundary that separates the hero from the body is the tightest on the page, by 9px.

findings.location: Overview grid, value column, rows Canonical (y832-874) and Finality (y874-915)
findings.finding: The two status badges have their box left edge at x=680 while every text value in the same column begins at x=689/690. The badge label is optically aligned but the badge box overhangs, so the value column's visible left edge ripples by 9px twice down six rows.

missing: hero: copy affordance on the full hash
raw section: the receipt payload, and labelling distinguishing transaction from receipt
decoded input: the 'supply an ABI' action (prose only, no control)

findings.location: hero, the H1 hash and the full hash line beneath it (y≈240–290)
findings.finding: No age and no finality badge appear in the hero — finality is only present as a 'Pending' row in the Overview grid — and neither the truncated H1 nor the full hash carries any copy affordance.

findings.location: Overview grid
findings.finding: The grid has six rows (Block, Canonical, Finality, Fee payer, Target, Cost · Mana). Value, nonce and transaction type are absent entirely.

findings.location: Raw (chain-native) section
findings.finding: The block contains only a five-line transaction-shaped object (aztec.kind, aztec.contract). The receipt payload is absent and the two payloads are neither labelled nor distinguishable, so 'transaction and receipt JSON verbatim' is not satisfied.

findings.location: Decoded input section, note panel below the selector/raw rows
findings.finding: The unknown-selector path renders the sentence 'Supplying an ABI decodes them.' but no 'supply an ABI' control — the specified action exists only as prose.

findings.location: trace card (hero, y≈340–615) vs Overview table vs Raw block
findings.finding: Three unrelated containment idioms on one page: the trace card has no border and is bounded only by a diffuse shadow; the Overview table and the Events/Internal-calls/State-changes panels use a ~#A2A2A2 1px hairline; the Raw block is a bare #ECECEB fill. There is no surface/elevation ladder, and the card carrying the primary action is the least-defined surface on the page.

findings.location: 'Succeeded' badge (hero) and 'Canonical: Yes' badge (Overview row 2) vs 'On demand' badge (trace card)
findings.finding: The page's single green role (#DCFCE7 / #166534) carries two different meanings — execution status and a boolean registry fact — while the trace-availability badge, the state the whole page turns on, is the only badge with no hue at all: a neutral dark dot on white with a hairline. Colour weight is allocated inversely to consequence.

findings.location: breadcrumb, 'TRANSACTION' eyebrow, Overview label column, the three explanation panels, footer
findings.finding: The text-emphasis ladder is compressed to #101010 / #242424 / #484848 / #565656. #484848 alone carries breadcrumb, eyebrow, grid labels, all explanatory prose and the footer, and #565656 is only 1.24:1 from it, so the last two levels are indistinguishable and colour does almost no hierarchy work.

findings.location: section rules between Overview / Decoded input / Events / Internal calls / State changes / Raw, and the header separator
findings.finding: Structural rules are #C8C8C8 on white — 1.86:1, below the 3:1 non-text floor — and the panel hairlines are ~2.6:1, so the page's containment is carried entirely by boundaries that are near-invisible on a bright display.

findings.location: whole page palette
findings.finding: The palette is stock framework values — pure neutral greys plus indigo-600 (#4F46E5) and green-100/800 — and the accent appears only twice (Generate trace fill, link colour). The theme reads as defaults not yet replaced rather than a designed light palette with an identity.

missing: hero: copy affordance on the full hash
hero: finality badge (Finality appears only as a grid row, not in the hero)
overview grid: fee breakdown (only a cost/limit usage row is shown)
decoded input: 'supply an ABI' action for the unknown selector
raw section: the chain-native receipt JSON

findings.location: hero (y≈240–290), overview grid (six rows, y≈795–1037), decoded-input section, raw section
findings.finding: Required facts are absent: the hero shows the full hash with no copy affordance and carries no age and no finality badge; the overview grid has only BLOCK, CANONICAL, FINALITY, FEE PAYER, TARGET and COST·MANA — no value, nonce, transaction type or fee breakdown; the decoded-input section states 'Supplying an ABI decodes them' in prose but offers no 'supply an ABI' control; the raw section shows one four-key transaction object and no receipt payload.

findings.location: whole page — content column spans x≈500–1415 of a 1920 px viewport
findings.finding: The wide viewport buys the page nothing. A single ~915 px column is used at every viewport, so roughly 1000 px of horizontal space is unused while the page runs to 2785 px vertically for about fifteen facts. The overview grid's value column is ~730 px wide to hold a 42-character address and a three-character 'Yes' badge; the decoded-input grid's value column holds '0x1a2b3c4d' and '0x' in the same 730 px. A two-column overview grid, or sections paired side by side, would put the whole factual payload in one screen.

findings.location: section separators between Overview, Decoded input, Events, Internal calls, State changes and Raw (rules at y≈707, 1135, 1504, 1752, 2010, 2256)
findings.finding: Section spacing is uniform regardless of section weight: each section ends ~100 px above its following rule and rules sit ~180–430 px apart whether the section holds a six-row table or a single sentence. Events, Internal calls and State changes are three near-identical one-sentence notices, each in a 700×~75 px card, spread across ~750 px of scroll — three facts for two-thirds of a screen. The gaps do not encode grouping, so the page reads as long rather than as structured.

findings.location: trace card (y≈348–608) and the Events / Internal calls / State changes notice cards versus the overview grid, decoded-input grid and raw block
findings.finding: Two content widths coexist in one scroll: the notice and trace cards end at x≈1195 while the grids, the raw block and the section rules run to x≈1405–1415. The 210 px difference leaves a ragged right edge on five of the eight sections and gives the eye no single right margin to scan against.

findings.location: decoded-input grid, RAW row (y≈1265)
findings.finding: The RAW row's value is the two characters '0x' — an empty calldata payload rendered as a full-height grid row. At realistic volume this section will hold a long hex string in the same cell, so this capture does not exercise the section's density case at all; a reviewer cannot judge the wrapping strategy from it.

missing: Hero: copy affordance on the full hash
Overview grid: fee breakdown (fee amount, not only mana cost/limit)

findings.location: hero, beside the truncated hash and the full hash line below it
findings.finding: The hero carries only a 'Succeeded' chip. Age is absent from the hero and from the entire page, the finality badge appears only as a row inside the Overview grid, and the full hash on the second line has no copy affordance.

findings.location: Overview grid
findings.finding: The grid has six rows (Block, Canonical, Finality, Fee payer, Target, Cost·Mana). Value, nonce and transaction type are absent, and there is no fee amount — only a mana cost/limit pair, which is the resource-usage requirement, not the fee breakdown.

findings.location: Decoded input section, notice panel below the Selector/Raw rows
findings.finding: For an unknown selector the spec requires raw bytes AND a 'supply an ABI' action. Only the sentence 'Supplying an ABI decodes them.' is present; there is no control to supply one, so the page describes an affordance it does not offer.

findings.location: Raw (chain-native) section
findings.finding: The block contains one four-line transaction object under an 'aztec' key. The receipt payload is absent and neither payload is labelled, so the section cannot be read as 'transaction and receipt, verbatim'.

findings.location: trace card (hero) versus the notice panels in Events, Internal calls and State changes
findings.finding: The page's primary action sits inside a bordered rounded panel that is the same shared primitive as the three 'nothing here yet' notices below it. The container that carries the product's most important control is visually indistinguishable from the container that carries its absences.

findings.location: trace card line 'Internal calls and state changes come from the execution trace.' versus the Internal calls and State changes panels
findings.finding: One fact, two vocabularies: the trace card says data 'comes from' the execution trace while both section panels say it is 'read from' it. The specified sentence is a shared primitive and its two paraphrases below make the page read as written by two hands.

findings.location: Events notice panel, and the trace card body copy
findings.finding: Internal architecture leaks into visitor-facing copy: 'once this chain's receipts are published to the data plane this page reads' (Events) and 'runs it again under the recorder' (trace card). Both name implementation surfaces a visitor has no model for, in a register that is otherwise plain-spoken.

findings.location: Raw (chain-native) section, the grey preformatted block
findings.finding: The one product-register element on the page is rendered as plain near-black monospace on a flat grey fill with no CodeTracer editor tokens, no panel header and no copy control. The product's single sanctioned register crossing is not made here, so the page's only code reads as an inert slab rather than as CodeTracer.

findings.location: trace card, primary button label 'Generate trace'
findings.finding: The primary action is labelled with a different verb from the product's signature 'Debug' used everywhere a transaction appears. The on-demand state justifies a distinct label, but nothing on the page ties 'Generate trace' back to debugging, so the page's strongest control does not read as the product's one promise.

findings.location: trace card body copy, clause 'it takes a moment, it needs an account'
findings.finding: Three unlike facts — a duration, an account requirement and a privacy claim — are strung into one sentence at equal weight, so the only one with a consequence for the visitor is the least prominent. 'A moment' is also the page's one unquantified quantity.

findings.location: footer, second line
findings.finding: 'Rendered from demo data (blocktracer-demo-gen)' sets the right honest tone but exposes an internal package name in monospace on a public surface; the human-readable half of the sentence already carries the meaning.

missing: Hero: copy affordance on the full hash
Hero: finality badge (rendered in the Overview grid instead)
Raw section: the chain-native receipt JSON (only a single unlabelled transaction object is shown)

findings.location: Overview section, the six-row fact grid below the trace card (y approx 790-1030)
findings.finding: The Overview grid carries six rows where Page-Descriptions 7.2 names eight facts: value, fee breakdown, nonce and transaction type are all absent, and their place is taken by CANONICAL and FINALITY badge rows (FINALITY being a hero requirement demoted into the grid). The omission is not a data limit - the raw block further down the page exposes "kind": "public-avm-call", so the transaction type is available and simply was never given a labelled row. The narrow 130px label column against an ~800px value column leaves every row two-thirds empty, confirming visually that the grid was populated from whatever the adapter exposed rather than from the specified fact set.

findings.location: identity bar, right group — 'Engine loading — 18 MB  128 / 1315'
findings.finding: The position readout is set in the proportional UI sans at the same size, weight and colour as the transient status string beside it, separated only by a space, so the debugger's single most-consulted number has no typographic identity and is read as the tail of a sentence. Its digits are also non-tabular ('128' averages ~9 px/char against '1315' at ~7 px/char), so the counter will reflow on every step.

findings.location: Transaction pane — 'EXECUTIONS' / 'DECODED INPUT' against 'BLOCK', 'FEE PAYER', 'SELECTOR', 'RAW'
findings.finding: Section headings and the field labels they contain use the same case, size (~12 px caps), weight, letterspacing and tone, so 'DECODED INPUT' reads as another field rather than as the group that owns SELECTOR and RAW. A level of hierarchy is missing from the densest pane on the page; only the pane title 'TRANSACTION' is separated, and by its grey band rather than by its type.

findings.location: page-wide — Call Trace 'ACIR opcodes' column vs identity-bar readout vs Values values column vs Transaction 'COST · MANA'
findings.finding: Four numeric conventions coexist: '1,315' (mono, grouped), '1315' (sans, ungrouped), '10000' / '9000' (mono, ungrouped) and '88000 / 200000' (mono, ungrouped). The number 1315 appears twice on the same screen in two different formats and two different faces. There is no single rule for magnitude grouping, so quantities cannot be compared across panes at a glance.

findings.location: Values pane, third column — 'Field', '[Field; 8]', 'u32'
findings.finding: The type column is proportional sans at ~12 px ('Field' averages 5.5 px/char) while the name and value columns in the same row are mono at ~14 px (7.7 px/char). Declared types are code tokens and are the one part of the row not set in the code face, so each row mixes two faces and the type column reads as UI chrome rather than as part of the value.

findings.location: Transaction pane, FEE PAYER and TARGET rows
findings.finding: 42-character addresses wrap mid-byte and strand a two-character widow — '32' and '4c' — alone on a right-aligned third line. Wrapping is not on a byte or fixed-column boundary, so the two addresses' lines do not align with each other and cannot be compared; a wrap rule at an even character count, or truncation with a copy affordance, would cost no information.

findings.location: Transaction pane — 'aztec private function executed client-side…' vs 'This selector is not in any ABI BlockTracer holds…'
findings.finding: Two body paragraphs in one pane at two sizes (~13 px and ~15 px). The larger of the two sits in the narrowest column on the page (~265 px), giving a measure of roughly 30 characters over six lines — the loosest, widest-set running text in the layout is in the place with least room for it, and it is not the more important of the two.

findings.location: Code pane, listing rows 26–56
findings.finding: Line pitch is ~23 px on ~13 px monospace, a ratio near 1.78, in a pane that has to announce it can only show from line 26. Roughly a third of the pane's vertical budget is leading. A debugger listing at desktop-app density runs nearer 1.4; tightening it adds rows rather than removing information.

findings.location: Code pane, right edge — lines 26, 40, 41, 42, 43
findings.finding: Long lines are cut mid-identifier ('remaining_shiel', 'each h', '/ 100;') behind a ~20 px fade, with no ellipsis and no horizontal scrollbar. The fade is too short to read as a deliberate truncation, so a clipped line is indistinguishable from a complete one — in a read-only listing where the reader is checking what the code actually says, that is the wrong default.

findings.location: Call Trace, FRAME column rows 4 and 7 — 'calculate_remaining_shie…  zk_shields · src/shi…'
findings.finding: Two ellipses per row at depth 3+, while the ACIR opcodes column to the right reserves roughly 90 px of width for values as short as '11'. The column is sized to its header string rather than to its widest value ('1,315'), and the frame names — the column the pane exists for — pay the difference.

findings.location: Values pane, 'masses' and 'masses[2]' rows
findings.finding: The array value wraps and its continuation is right-aligned, so the closing bracket floats alone at the right edge on line two and the array reads as two unrelated fragments; array values should stay left-aligned once they wrap, unlike the scalars above and below. The child row 'masses[2]' is then indented only ~8 px — one character — from its siblings, below the depth at which indentation reads as nesting rather than as a stray space.

findings.location: identity bar, second line — 'Share' and 'Download trace'
findings.finding: The two secondary actions carry the heaviest weight in the identity bar — heavier than the transaction hash above them and heavier than the position readout. Weight is inverted relative to importance; the bar's own subject is set lighter than the buttons that act on it.

findings.location: Code pane, notice above line 26 — 'Showing from line 26 — the session's position is below…'
findings.finding: Chrome prose is set in the editor monospace at the listing's own size, so it reads as a comment in the source rather than as an explanation of the window. Setting it in the UI sans one step down would separate it from the code it describes.

findings.location: Transaction pane badges — 'Partial', 'Yes', 'Safe', 'Not observable', 'Trace ready'
findings.finding: Five badges on one pane use three label treatments: mono ('Partial'), sans regular ('Yes', 'Safe', 'Not observable') and sans bold ('Trace ready'). The face and weight differences do not encode anything, so they read as three unrelated badge components rather than one primitive in three states.

findings.location: Call Trace, header row — 'FRAME' and 'ACIR opcodes'
findings.finding: One header strip carries two casing conventions: all-caps on the left, mixed-case on the right. The pane's own tab labels and every other pane title on the page are all-caps, so the right-hand header is the only exception.

findings.location: top of the Call Trace / Event Log tabbed region, middle column (x 686-1144, y 87-111)
findings.finding: The middle column's pane top edge is at y=111 while the Code and Transaction panes both start at y=87, leaving a 24px-tall empty white band across the full width of the middle column between the identity-bar rule (y=82) and the tabbed region. The top edge of the three-column grid therefore has a visible step in it, and the three pane titles are on two baselines: CODE and TRANSACTION glyphs occupy y=95-103, CALL TRACE occupies y=119-127. Their header bottom rules land at y=113, y=113 and y=138.

findings.location: Call Trace region, below the 'Sorted by call order. / Sort by cost' footer (y 365-577)
findings.finding: MEASUREMENT requested by the watch-for. The tabbed region spans y=111-578 (467px). Its seven frames end at the last row rule y=344 and the footer strip ends at y=365. From y=365 to the pane's bottom border at y=577 there are 212px of blank pane — 45% of the region. The Values pane below it (y=583-895, 312px) holds ten rows ending at y=877, i.e. it is filled to within 18px of its own border and its 'masses' row already wraps to two lines. The Values pane is the one that should have the height; roughly 150px of the void belongs to it. Counting the 24px notch in finding 1, 30% of the middle column's 784px is empty.

findings.location: identity bar, both rows (y 0-82)
findings.finding: The bar's vertical padding is 0 / 32 / 0. The stepping-button group's top edge is at y=0, flush against the viewport top with no padding at all, while the bar carries 24px of left padding. The wrapped second row (NOIR, Share, Download trace) has 32px of empty space above it (y=27 to y=60) and none below: its button borders end at y=81 and the full-width divider rule is at y=82, so they butt straight into it. The two rows read as two unrelated strips rather than one bar that wrapped.

findings.location: identity bar content edges vs the pane grid (x=24 / x=1378 vs x=4 / x=1435)
findings.finding: Nothing in the identity bar lines up with the column grid it sits above. Both bar rows start their content at x=24 ('back to aztec' and 'NOIR'), while the Code pane's left border is at x=4 — a 20px offset. On the right the phase rail's pill cap ends at x=1378 while the Transaction pane's border reaches x=1435, a 57px offset. That is three different left/right edges inside the top 90px of the page.

findings.location: Code pane left gutter (x 8-46) and right edge (x 674-686)
findings.finding: 40px of the Code pane's left gutter carries nothing while seven of the thirty-one visible lines lose their tails at the right edge. The gutter runs: pane border x=4, current-line accent bar x=6, line numbers x=46-62, marker dot x=78, code column zero x=96 — so x=8 to x=46 is empty, and the total gutter is 92px of a 683px pane (13.5%). Meanwhile lines 26, 40, 41, 42, 48, 49 and 53 are cut mid-token at x~674 with no ellipsis and no visible horizontal scrollbar ('...(initial_shield, re', 'after each h', 'remaining_shi'). Reclaiming ~34px of gutter returns about four characters per line.

findings.location: Transaction pane, FEE PAYER and TARGET rows (y 327-517)
findings.finding: The value column is about nine pixels too narrow, so every 42-character address wraps to three lines with a two-character orphan. The value column is x=1260-1427 = 167px = 20 monospace characters; 42 characters need 21 per line to fit in two. The result is two full lines plus '32' alone on the third for FEE PAYER and '4c' alone for TARGET, costing ~24px of pane height each. The label column reserves 103px for a longest label ('CANONICAL') that measures 72px, so the nine pixels are available without touching the pane width.

findings.location: Transaction pane, identity block (y 113-263) vs FEE PAYER / TARGET rows
findings.finding: The same content type is aligned two different ways in one pane. The full transaction hash under the Partial badge is left-aligned at x=1157 and uses the pane's full 270px width; the FEE PAYER and TARGET addresses — identical 42-character hex — are right-aligned into the 167px value column. 'Status reason: private-part-succeeded-public-part-succeeded' is likewise left-aligned full-width while every other value in the pane is right-aligned to x=1427. The pane reads as two stacked layouts rather than one column list.

findings.location: Transaction pane, BLOCK row (y ~246-263)
findings.finding: Proximity groups BLOCK with the wrong thing. The first hairline-bounded cell (y=113-263) contains the badge, the truncated hash, the two-line full hash, the two-line status reason AND the 'BLOCK 101:0' row, with no rule between the status reason and BLOCK. Rules do separate CANONICAL (y=263-295) and FINALITY (y=295-327), which are the same label:value shape as BLOCK. So the one row that most resembles its two neighbours is fenced inside the identity block instead of starting the list.

findings.location: Values pane, 'masses[2]' row (x=708) against the Call Trace indent above it
findings.finding: Two nesting indents on two different scales, 200px apart in the same column. In the Values pane 'masses[2]' is inset to x=708 while 'masses', 'mass', 'initial_shield' and 'i' are flush at x=702 — a 6px step, half a monospace character, too small to read as nesting and large enough to read as a broken left edge, and with no guide. Directly above it the Call Trace expresses depth with a ~16px step plus a vertical guide rail (though that rail sits at a fixed x=706 and does not multiply with depth, so depths 2 and 3 are indented but unguided).

findings.location: Code pane, file-tab strip (x=22) vs the CODE label (x=13) and the 'Showing from line 26' note (x=14)
findings.finding: Three stacked strips in one pane sit on two left edges. The pane title 'CODE' starts at x=13 and the position note below the tabs starts at x=14, but the file tabs (Nargo.toml / Prover.toml / src/main.nr / src/shield.nr) start at x=22 — an unexplained 8px step in and back out again.

findings.location: identity bar, phase rail, left cap of the active FETCHING segment (x ~1222-1232, y 3-24)
findings.finding: The active segment's fill does not follow the pill's radius: the blue FETCHING fill has a square left edge inside the pill's rounded left cap, leaving a 2-3px white crescent between the border and the fill. The other two segments are square-ended and unaffected, so only the leftmost, currently-active one shows the seam.

findings.location: Values pane, 'masses' row (y 685-726)
findings.finding: The array literal is right-aligned and wraps, leaving '14]' alone on a second line beneath the middle of line one with no left anchor to sit under, and making the row 41px tall against the 25px of every other row in the pane. Either give the array the row's full width with a hanging indent at the value column's left edge, or truncate it as the Call Trace truncates frame names.

findings.location: Values pane, change markers on the 'remaining_shield' and 'damage' rows (x 693-696)
findings.finding: The blue changed-value bar sits at x=693-696 while the pane's left border is at x=691, so it visually touches the border rather than sitting inside the 9px content inset that every other element in the pane respects. Two pixels of clearance reads as a rendering seam on the border rather than as a marker in the gutter.

findings.location: whole page — identity bar / canvas / pane bodies / pane headers; gutters between the Code, Call Trace and Transaction columns
findings.finding: The light theme has no surface ladder. The identity bar, the page canvas, every pane body and the pane header fills (CODE, CALL TRACE, VALUES, TRANSACTION) sit within two near-white tones, so panes are distinguished only by a hairline and the boundary between chrome and content at the identity bar is carried by position alone rather than by surface. Introduce a genuine three-step ratchet — canvas darker than pane, pane header a third step — so the light theme is designed rather than the dark theme's elevation inverted.

findings.location: identity bar (`← aztec`), Transaction pane (`101:0`), Call Trace footer (`Sort by cost`), Code pane line 32 marker, Call Trace row 6, Values rows `remaining_shield`/`damage`, Code pane keywords
findings.finding: One accent blue carries four unrelated meanings on a single screen: hyperlink, current position, changed-since-previous-step value, and code keyword token. A reader cannot tell from hue whether blue means 'go here', 'you are here' or 'this changed'. The collision is worst in the Values pane, where blue numerals (9000, 2000) sit six rows below a blue link in the pane above.

findings.location: identity bar, phase rail — `OPENING` and `POSITIONING` chips right of the active `FETCHING`
findings.finding: The two pending phase chips are pale grey uppercase at roughly 10px on white, well under the contrast floor. The phase rail is the honesty surface for engine loading, so the phases that have not happened yet must still be readable as named phases; at this contrast they degrade into texture and the rail reads as one chip plus noise.

findings.location: identity bar, stepping control cluster (the seven buttons between `block 101` and the scrubber)
findings.finding: All stepping buttons render as the same mid-grey glyph in the same hairline-bordered chip, so there is no legible enabled/disabled split while the engine is still FETCHING. The expectation makes the buttons' disabled state one of the carriers of the loading state now that the prose band is gone; with no tonal difference between an available step and an unavailable one, that state is not being carried by anything the eye can read.

findings.location: Code pane, comment on line 41 (`// shields regain a percentage of the maxium capacity...`)
findings.finding: The comment token is a pale salmon on white — the lowest-contrast text in the Code pane and below the floor at this size, despite being the only prose in the listing. It is also the only red-family colour on the page, in a product where red is the reverted/failed role; a de-emphasised comment should not be the page's sole red. Darken the comment token for light surfaces and move it off the failure hue.

findings.location: Code pane, row shading across lines 26–55
findings.finding: Alternating rows carry a light grey fill that does not follow a clean two-row cycle (26 and 27 are both shaded, 30 and 31 are both clear), so it is not readable as zebra striping and not readable as executed-line coverage either. The grey is the same value as the pane-header fill, so shaded runs also read faintly as heading bands. Either commit the grey to a state role and make it distinguishable from the header tone, or make it a true zebra.

findings.location: identity bar, scrubber between the stepping cluster and `Engine loading — 18 MB`
findings.finding: The scrubber's filled portion and its empty track differ by a very light grey, and the striped hatch reads as a texture rather than as a fill level, so position within the 1315-opcode trace is not legible from colour at all — the `128 / 1315` readout beside it is doing the entire job. The one element required to express position within the trace is the lowest-contrast element in the bar.

findings.location: Transaction pane pills (`Yes`, `Safe`, `Not observable`, `Trace ready`) and the `NOIR` pill in the identity bar
findings.finding: The grey outline pill means three different things — a taxonomy label (NOIR), affirmative facts (Yes, Safe) and a capability limitation (Not observable) — while `Trace ready`, also an affirmative fact, is the page's only green. Green appears once and grey spans an affirmative and its opposite, so pill colour is not a role a reader can learn. Amber `Partial` is used consistently in both places and is the one pill colour that works.

findings.location: Transaction pane — small-caps labels (BLOCK, CANONICAL, FEE PAYER), explanatory prose ('aztec private function executed client-side...', 'This selector is not in any ABI...') and the right-hand type column in Values (Field, u32)
findings.finding: Three greys are in play for three different jobs — label, secondary prose, and unit/type annotation — but they sit close enough in value that they read as one de-emphasised level. Either separate them by a clear step or collapse them to two intentional levels.

findings.location: middle column, Call Trace tabbed region (x 691-1144, y 110-578)
findings.finding: The measurement the Watch-for asks for: the region is 468 px tall and carries 253 px of content — last ink is the 'Sorted by call order / Sort by cost' footer at y=363, the region floor is y=578, so 214 px (46% of the region, 24% of the viewport height) is blank below the last frame. Nothing in the column needs it: Values below closes cleanly after `i` at y=868 with all ten values shown. The height should go left or right, not to this region — the Code pane is fading eight lines at its right edge and the Transaction pane is running off the bottom of the viewport. Row pitch compounds it: frames sit on a 25 px pitch for ~13 px glyphs (y=176, 201, 226, 251, 277, 302, 327), so the blank space is 8 more frames' worth at a pitch that is already loose for this register.

findings.location: Call Trace rows, frame column (x 700-1050)
findings.finding: Every one of the seven frames repeats the invariant crate name `zk_shields`, and it is that repetition that consumes the width the deep frames need: the two depth-3 rows at y=251 and y=327 both truncate to `calculate_remaining_shie… zk_shields · src/shi…` and are now character-for-character identical although they are different frames. The one token that would tell them apart is the one in the ellipsis, and the constant that survives is the one that identifies nothing. Hoist `zk_shields` to the pane header or drop it where it matches the parent frame.

findings.location: identity bar, second row (y 55-88)
findings.finding: The bar wraps at 1440: row one ends with the phase rail at x≈1380, and NOIR / Share / Download trace drop to a second row occupying x=14-250. There is no ink at all from x=400 to x=1440 on that row — 33 px of viewport height for three objects, 83% of it empty — on a page where the Transaction pane is already cut off at the fold. Either the two actions fit row one (they need ~200 px; 'Engine loading — 18 MB' and the language tag are the compressible neighbours) or the wrapped row should not cost a full row of height.

findings.location: Transaction pane, header block (y 120-185)
findings.finding: The transaction hash renders twice inside 60 px — truncated as `0xb636167a…66d46359` beside the Partial badge at y=129, then in full across two wrapped lines at y=155-180 — and a third time in the identity bar at y=14. Three renderings of one value, costing three of the pane's ~30 visible rows, in the narrowest (286 px) and most content-starved pane on the page. Keep the full value and drop the truncated echo; the badge does not need a hash beside it when the full one is on the next line.

findings.location: Transaction pane, FEE PAYER (y 340-390) and TARGET (y 411-460)
findings.finding: Both 66-character addresses wrap right-aligned over three lines with a two-character orphan on the last (`32` and `4c`). Right-aligned wrapped hex cannot be read as one token — the eye has to re-find the left edge on each line, the ragged left is different for each value, and the orphan line reads as a separate right-aligned field rather than the tail of the address. Left-align the wrapped value under its own first character, or truncate to head/tail with the full value on copy as the identity bar already does.

findings.location: Transaction pane, DECODED INPUT rows and the note below them (y 690-830)
findings.finding: SELECTOR and RAW both render as a bare `0x` with no bytes after it, which is indistinguishable from a value that failed to load or was truncated, and they are followed by five lines of proportional-face prose — 'This selector is not in any ABI BlockTracer holds, so the parameters are shown as raw bytes' — that describes bytes the rows do not contain. That is ~110 px, roughly an eighth of the pane's visible height, spent saying there is no calldata, in the densest pane at the narrowest column, while the raw chain-native JSON below it gets one visible `{` before the fold. Say 'no calldata' in the value slot and cut the note to one line.

findings.location: identity bar, back link at x 30-100
findings.finding: The backbone names 'a link back to the transaction detail page'; the only link-styled element in the bar is `← aztec`, which reads as the chain overview, and the truncated hash beside it carries no static link affordance. Not scored P1 because §7.0 serves a metadata page only for a transaction with no session — this one has one — and the Transaction pane satisfies the 'identity reachable' item. Worth a decision on whether the arrow's destination matches what the arrow promises.

findings.location: identity bar, scrubber (x 690-845)
findings.finding: The one element expressing position within a 1315-step trace is 155 px wide — the narrowest object in a bar that ends with 55 px of trailing slack and a mostly empty second row. At ~8.5 steps per pixel the ticks cannot express the position; all the precision is carried by the adjacent `128 / 1315` readout, which makes the strip decoration. Widening it is the density-positive direction, so it is a finding rather than a tension, but the ranking argument for keeping the controls dominant is understood — hence P3.

findings.location: Values pane, all rows (name column ends x≈805, value column starts x≈1000)
findings.finding: Every row has a ~195 px void between the identifier and its right-aligned value (`initial_shield` … `10000`, `shield_regen_percentage` … `10`), with no leader and no zebra. Right-alignment against the type column is correct for scanning a column of magnitudes, but at 453 px of pane width the name-to-value association is carried by the 25 px row pitch alone. This is the pane that has spare width because the region above it has spare height.

findings.location: Code pane, bottom edge (y≈895)
findings.finding: The pane height is not a multiple of the 23 px line pitch, so line 56 is bisected by the pane's own bottom border — the glyphs of `// in noir, fields can't be printed directly…` are cut through the middle by the rounded frame rather than scrolled out of it. It reads as clipping rather than as a scroll position. Snap the listing's visible height to the line grid.

findings.location: Code pane, between the file tab strip and line 26
findings.finding: The pane narrates its own viewport in a full-width sentence — "Showing from line 26 — the session's position is below, and the lines above it are not in this window." No code editor explains where its own scroll position is, and the desktop app says this with the gutter and the scrollbar. It is the same species of page-level explanation as the engine-notice band removed on 2026-08-29, relocated one level down into the flagship pane; the current line is already unmistakable six rows below it.

findings.location: Code pane, listing rows lines 30-56
findings.finding: The code listing is zebra-striped in alternating light-grey and white bands. Row striping is the explorer's data-table primitive from blocks-list and txs-list; §3 sanctions exactly one register crossing — editor tokens into explorer pages — and this is the reverse of it. It also puts a second horizontal banding signal underneath the executed-line dots and the current-line band, so the pane's own position language competes with table furniture.

findings.location: Call Trace footer ("Sort by cost") and TRANSACTION pane BLOCK row ("101:0")
findings.finding: In-pane controls are drawn with the explorer's link primitive — accent-blue, underlined, proportional, body-size. In the desktop app a sort is a column-header affordance and a block target is a chip or a mono value; a hyperlink inside a tool pane reads as web chrome dropped into the session and makes two different interaction types (re-sort, navigate away) look identical.

findings.location: identity bar, second row (NOIR / Share / Download trace)
findings.finding: The bar carries two button vocabularies: the stepping cluster is square, tight-padded, grey tool buttons, while Share and Download trace are rounded pills with marketing-grade horizontal padding. The wrap to a second row is a stated decision, but the row is left-aligned with roughly 1100 px of empty canvas to its right and no rule or label, so the deliberate "page actions" row reads as an orphaned toolbar strip in explorer clothing rather than as the second half of one bar.

findings.location: TRANSACTION pane, line below the full hash
findings.finding: "Status reason: private-part-succeeded-public-part-succeeded" prints an internal enum slug verbatim as a status sentence, and its inline sentence-case label conflicts with the uppercase label column (BLOCK, CANONICAL, FINALITY, FEE PAYER) used by every other row in the same pane. Two label vocabularies in one pane, and the product's copy register is broken by a machine identifier presented as prose.

findings.location: tabbed Call Trace region, area below the footer strip (y≈370-577)
findings.finding: The region is ~470 px tall; its seven frames end at y≈345 and the "Sorted by call order." footer sits at y≈357, leaving ~207 px — about 44% of the region — as empty white inside the pane border, below its own footer. The Values pane beneath it is filled but not starved, so at this fixture the slack should go to Values or the region should size to its content; a tool register cannot spend nearly half of its primary navigation surface on nothing.

findings.location: identity bar, scrubber immediately left of "Engine loading — 18 MB"
findings.finding: The scrubber renders as a short filled segment against a long dotted track and abuts the words "Engine loading — 18 MB", so the position indicator reads as a 10%-complete engine download meter. The status is truthful about the engine and the panes are honestly a positioned first frame, but the adjacency turns a trace-position control into an apparent progress bar for a different quantity. Put the status before the controls, or label the track.

findings.location: identity bar hash vs TRANSACTION pane hash
findings.finding: One hash is rendered three ways on one screen and with two truncation rules: 0xb63616…6359 (6+4) in the bar, 0xb636167a…66d46359 (8+8) beside the Partial badge, and the full value wrapped over two lines directly beneath that. The pane's truncated form has no job when the full value sits under it, and a single truncation rule across registers is a shared primitive worth holding.

findings.location: TRANSACTION pane, EXECUTIONS note and DECODED INPUT note
findings.finding: Both honesty notes ("aztec private function executed client-side; …no call structure to trace" and "This selector is not in any ABI BlockTracer holds…") are set in proportional sans at explorer body size and leading inside the densest column of the tool. The content is right and should stay; the typography is the tx-detail page's, so the pane reads as a slice of the explorer pasted into the session. Re-set at label/mono scale rather than shortened.

findings.location: identity bar, status cluster between the scrubber and the NOIR/Share actions — "Engine loading — 18 MB" plus the phase rail (FETCHING lit, OPENING and POSITIONING unlit)
findings.finding: The status readout and phase rail announce a session that is still fetching and has not yet been opened or positioned, while the rest of the page shows a fully positioned session: position 128 / 1315, current line 32 highlighted in Code, seven resolved call-trace frames with opcode counts, twelve populated Values rows, and stepping controls rendered active rather than disabled. The page reports a different state from the one it is displaying, so the one element that is supposed to tell the user whether the panes are live is the element contradicting them.

findings.location: Transaction pane, FEE PAYER and TARGET value rows
findings.finding: Both 40-hex addresses wrap mid-byte onto a second, right-aligned line (0x01c8f081e2abedf0184953e2a272b5 / e430d5d932 and 0x1b31c04d5920b0b5936f12e6fe8f17 / a59161624c) with no ellipsis, no separator and no signal that the two lines are one value. The brief names truncation mid-byte as the failing example of hash treatment. Every other value row in the pane is a single line, so these two also break the row rhythm.

findings.location: Call Trace opcode column vs Values pane vs Transaction pane COST · MANA row
findings.finding: Thousands separators are applied only in the Call Trace ACIR column (1,315 / 1,208); the same magnitudes appear unseparated in Values (10000, 9000, 2000, 1000) and in COST · MANA (88000 / 200000). One page shows two numeral conventions for comparable magnitudes, so the reader cannot judge scale at a glance across panes.

findings.location: Call Trace pane, module/file path beside each frame name
findings.finding: The qualifier 'zk_shields · src/shield.nr' is the smallest and lowest-emphasis type on the page (~10 px), yet it is the only thing distinguishing the two calculate_damage frames (rows 3 and 6) and the two calculate_remaining_shield_pct frames (rows 4 and 7) from one another. The disambiguator is set below the ambiguous label, which inverts the hierarchy exactly where a deep trace needs it.

findings.location: Identity bar, centre — 'Engine loading — 18 MB' and '128 / 1315' against the hash at the far left
findings.finding: The transient loading status and the byte counter are set at the same size and the same brightness as the transaction hash 0xb63616…6359, so the loudest text in the bar is the text that disappears when the session finishes loading. Identity should outrank status by at least one level of size or weight.

findings.location: Identity bar, full width
findings.finding: Four case conventions share a 44 px strip with no rule mapping case to role: 'block 101' lowercase sans, 'Partial' title-case pill, 'FETCHING / OPENING / POSITIONING' and 'NOIR' uppercase letterspaced, 'Share' / 'Download trace' title case. Because case is not carrying a consistent meaning, the bar reads as a row of unrelated objects rather than as grouped identity, controls, status and actions.

findings.location: Code pane lines 40, 53 and 64; Transaction pane RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE) block, "contract" line
findings.finding: Long lines stop dead at the container's right edge with no ellipsis, fade or visible scroll affordance: line 40 ends at 'shield_regen_perce', line 53 at 'damage: Field, r', and the raw JSON is cut at '"contract": "0x1b31c04d5920b0b5936f12' with no closing quote. Nothing on screen tells the reader whether the value continues or ended, which is the one thing a truncation treatment exists to say.

findings.location: Transaction pane, DECODED INPUT — SELECTOR and RAW rows
findings.finding: Both values render as the bare prefix '0x' with no digits, immediately above prose stating that the parameters are shown as raw bytes. Set in the same bright mono as real values, '0x' reads as a truncation that removed everything rather than as a stated absence; an empty value needs a word, not a prefix.

findings.location: Code pane, note line above line 26
findings.finding: 'Showing from line 26 — the session's position is below, and the lines above it are not in this window.' runs the full ~890 px pane width as a single ~110-character line in the UI sans, inside an otherwise monospace listing. At this measure the eye has to track back across the whole pane, and it is the only sans prose in the pane.

findings.location: Call Trace pane, column header row
findings.finding: 'FRAME' is uppercase and letterspaced while its opposite number is 'ACIR opcodes' — an uppercase token followed by a lowercase word. One header row uses two treatments, so 'ACIR opcodes' reads as a caption rather than as the peer of FRAME.

findings.location: Transaction pane, top two lines
findings.finding: The truncated pill 0x636167a…66d46359 sits directly above the full 0x636167a05b9de55bde67756bdaed6e766d46359 on the next line. The pane's two brightest mono lines carry the same value, so the truncation buys no space and instead costs a level of hierarchy at the top of the pane.

findings.location: Transaction pane, 'Status reason' line
findings.finding: 'private-part-succeeded-public-part-succeeded' wraps at an internal hyphen, breaking as 'public-part-' / 'succeeded'. A machine identifier broken at a hyphen at the line end is indistinguishable from typographic hyphenation, so the reader cannot tell whether the trailing hyphen is part of the value.

findings.location: Transaction pane, EXECUTIONS section
findings.finding: The sub-labels 'private' and 'public' are lowercase sans and share their left edge with the uppercase letterspaced section labels (BLOCK, CANONICAL, FINALITY, EXECUTIONS, DECODED INPUT). Sharing the edge makes them read as peers of the section labels in a different case rather than as a level below them.

findings.location: Call Trace pane, selected frame row `calculate_damage` (y≈287)
findings.finding: Marking the current frame cuts its contrast by four times. On the #312e81 selection fill the frame name is #818cf8 (3.83:1) and the module path `zk_shields · src/shield.nr` is #919191 (3.62:1) — both below 4.5:1 — while the identical text one row up on #1b1b1b runs 15.52:1 and 5.47:1. Only the opcode count (#dddddd, 8.41:1) survives. The Code pane paints its current line with the same #312e81 fill but keeps #f3f3f3 on it at 10.29:1, so the two panes that share the selection fill disagree on its foreground. The current position is therefore the single hardest row to read in the pane that exists to show it.

findings.location: identity bar back-link, Code pane line 32 gutter, Call Trace selected row and footer link, Values pane rows `remaining_shield`/`damage`, Transaction pane `101:0`
findings.finding: One indigo carries four unrelated roles. #818cf8 is the link colour (`← aztec`, `Sort by cost`, `101:0`), the current-position colour (2px left rail, line number and `▶` caret on code line 32; 2px left rail and name on the selected frame), the diff/changed-value colour (2px left rail plus the numerals `9000` and `2000` in Values), and — through #312e81 and #a5b4fc — the in-progress status colour (`FETCHING` badge fill, scrubber head). The visible cost is in the Values pane: every other numeral there is #dddddd, so the two changed values are the only coloured text in the pane and they are painted in precisely the hue used for hyperlinks two panes to the right. Position and diff are different questions and must not share a swatch with navigation.

findings.location: Transaction pane chips (`Partial`, `Yes`, `Safe`, `Not observable`, `Trace ready`) and the eight stepping buttons in the identity bar (x≈396–670)
findings.finding: The chip/button fill #202020 sits 1.06:1 against the #1b1b1b pane (ΔL* 1.3, at or under the just-noticeable threshold), so none of these components has a visible body — each is held only by its 1px border. That border is itself inconsistent in weight: `Partial` (#ea580c, 4.58:1) and `Trace ready` (#16a34a, 4.94:1) read as real chips, while `Yes`, `Safe` and `Not observable` are outlined at roughly 1.5:1 and read as loose grey text. One component renders as two different things within a single pane, and the stepping buttons read as bare glyphs rather than a grouped control cluster.

findings.location: identity bar, stepping control group (x≈396–670, y≈20–46)
findings.finding: All eight stepping glyphs are exactly #818181 on #202020 = 4.18:1 — measured button by button, not one is brighter or dimmer than another. Two consequences. First, reverse stepping, which the expectation block calls this product's entire premise, is the lowest-contrast element in the bar it is required to be visible in: the hash beside it is 15.52:1, `Download trace` 15.52:1, `Engine loading — 18 MB` 12.68:1. Second, with the engine at `FETCHING` the block names the buttons' disabled state as one of the three carriers of loading status, but since every glyph is one value there is no disabled state to read.

findings.location: identity bar, position scrubber (x≈686–952, y≈22–42)

findings.location: Transaction pane, CANONICAL / FINALITY / EXECUTIONS rows (y≈227–279 and y≈446–464) against the `public` row (y≈535)

Colour-by-exception is a defensible policy, but the neutral currently spans an affirmation and a limitation in one pane.

findings.location: whole surface — greyscale ramp and accent set

The accents consequently float on a base that shares no hue with them, and the two families near-collide where they meet: comment green #22c55e beside chip green #4ade80, string orange #fdba74 and call amber #fbbf24 beside `Partial` orange #fb923c, numeric-literal violet #c4b5fd beside position indigo #818cf8. It reads as a default palette adopted rather than a theme designed.

findings.location: Code pane body and its right edge (x≈916–921); pane header strips; Transaction pane RAW block

findings.location: identity bar, phase rail `OPENING` / `POSITIONING` (x≈1318–1480)

findings.location: Code pane, right edge (x≈915), lines 40, 53, 56 and 64

findings.location: navigation column — Call Trace tabbed region (y 93–673) versus Values pane (y 683–1078)

findings.location: identity bar, centre cluster (scrubber x 688–955, 'Engine loading — 18 MB' x 963–1120, '128 / 1315' x 1130–1220)

findings.location: Transaction pane, FEE PAYER and TARGET rows (y 299–380)

findings.location: Transaction pane, DECODED INPUT block (SELECTOR / RAW rows and the paragraph at y 650–710)

findings.location: Call Trace pane, frame rows y 155–320 (path suffixes and the 'ACIR opcodes' header)

findings.location: identity bar, stepping controls (x 390–670)

findings.location: Code pane header stack (y 68–155)

findings.location: Values pane header (y 697)

findings.location: Values pane, `masses` row (y 798) and `masses[2]` row (y 823)

missing: Identity bar: a link back to the transaction detail page. The only link is '← aztec', which is labelled with the chain and routes to the chain overview; the truncated hash '0xb63616…6359' carries none of this page's link treatment (periwinkle + underline).

findings.location: identity bar, far left (x≈28–160, y=31)
findings.finding: No link back to the transaction detail page. The bar's only navigational affordance is '← aztec', styled as a link and labelled with the chain, so it reads and behaves as 'back to the aztec chain'. The truncated hash beside it is plain white monospace while every real link on the page (← aztec, 101:0, Sort by cost) is periwinkle and underlined, so by the page's own vocabulary the hash is inert. The debug route is a deliberate register crossing and the way back across it — to /aztec/tx/0xb636…, which Page-Descriptions §7.0 keeps as a distinct address — is not rendered. The implementation's comment argues the link had become a self-link; §7.0 says the two addresses 'differ in what the visitor asked for', and the non-debug one is the crawlable, canonical, explorer-register surface, so it is not a self-link. Carried unresolved from round 4.

findings.location: Transaction pane, third row, beneath the full hash
findings.finding: 'Status reason: private-part-succeeded-public-part-succeeded' ships a raw enum identifier as user-facing prose in the flagship pane. Every other string on this surface is product English; this one is a serialised symbol, hyphen-joined and wrapped over two lines. The debugger register is dense, not internal — a CodeTracer user reads the tool's language, not its state machine's. Render it as the two facts it encodes (private part succeeded, public part succeeded), ideally as the same badge pair already used two rows below for 'Not observable' and 'Trace ready'.

findings.location: CODE pane, full-width row beneath the file tab strip (y≈139)
findings.finding: 'Showing from line 26 — the session's position is below, and the lines above it are not in this window.' is explorer-register narration inside the densest pane of the tool register. It is a chatty sentence in the body voice, in a pane whose every other row is a gutter number and a token. The desktop app expresses a windowed listing structurally — an elision marker in the gutter, a dimmed rule at the window edge — not with a sentence explaining it. It is also the same species of furniture as the full-width loading band §8 removed on 2026-08-29, re-grown one level down: prose elsewhere on the page explaining a condition the object itself should draw.

findings.location: identity bar, right group (Share / Download trace, x≈1720–1910)
findings.finding: The loudest object in the bar is the solid light-filled 'Download trace' pill — the explorer register's primary-CTA treatment, and the only filled button on the surface — given to a file download. The product's stated premise, reverse stepping, is eight small unlabelled glyphs at 40% of that contrast. The bar's emphasis therefore ranks a utility action above the controls the spec deliberately moved here to keep permanently on screen, which inverts the ranking that move was made to express.

findings.location: identity bar, control group (x≈395–670)
findings.finding: The stepping controls speak a media-transport vocabulary (◀ ▶, ⏮ ⏭) plus four ambiguous arrow glyphs, with no labels, no keyboard hints and no textual anchor. Reverse stepping is present as the spec demands, but a CodeTracer desktop user cannot map this row onto the named commands they already know — nothing distinguishes 'step back over' from 'step out'. B9 asks for the same control vocabulary as the desktop app; this is a video player's. Placement is a sanctioned divergence and is not the issue; the iconography is.

findings.location: Transaction pane, rows CANONICAL / FINALITY / EXECUTIONS (y≈235–545)
findings.finding: One badge primitive carries five different kinds of meaning within a single pane: an outcome (orange 'Partial'), a boolean ('Yes' for CANONICAL), a classification ('Safe' for FINALITY), an observability state ('Not observable'), and a readiness state (green 'Trace ready'). 'Yes' is the weakest — a plain boolean promoted into a chip while the rows above and below it render bare values right-aligned, so the badge stops signalling 'this is a status' and becomes decoration. Reserve the pill for status and let booleans be values.

findings.location: CALL TRACE pane — column header row (y≈135) and footer row (y≈338)
findings.finding: Three casing conventions in one pane: the pane and column labels are uppercase micro-labels ('CALL TRACE', 'FRAME'), the adjacent column header mixes an uppercase acronym with a lowercase word ('ACIR opcodes'), and the footer is sentence case with a terminal full stop ('Sorted by call order.') beside a sentence-case link ('Sort by cost'). Pick one voice for pane chrome; the uppercase micro-label is the one the rest of the surface uses.

findings.location: whole workspace — gutters between CODE, CALL TRACE/VALUES and TRANSACTION columns
findings.finding: The session is built as separated rounded cards floating on a page background rather than as the contiguous, gutter-less workspace split by sashes that is the desktop app's pane vocabulary. The idiom reads as a web dashboard. It is defensible at 1920 and the pane headers are consistent, but VD.5 exists to record divergences from the desktop app and this is the structural one; it should be a deliberate, written-down choice rather than an inherited web default.

findings.location: identity bar, status group (x≈960–1490)

Fold the size into the active phase chip, or set the two in one voice.

findings.location: navigation column — Call Trace region below the 'Sorted by call order.' footer, and Values pane below the 'i' row

findings.location: Code pane, right edge (x=913) — lines 40, 53, 56, 63, 64

findings.location: identity bar, full width
findings.finding: Six functional clusters — identity, stepping controls, scrubber, 'Engine loading / 128 / 1315', phase rail — are separated by a uniform 15-22px (17, 17, 22, 18, 15), then a single 189px gap before NOIR/Share/Download trace. findings.location: Transaction pane, FEE PAYER and TARGET rows

findings.location: Code pane, header strips (y=65 to y=152)
findings.finding: Three stacked full-width strips — the CODE title (28px), the file-tab row (28px) and the 'Showing from line 26' note (31px) — consume 87px before the first code row, roughly four code rows' worth, in a pane whose listing is already clipped at the right edge and the fold.

findings.location: Code pane, left edges — CODE title x=14, file-tab row x=21, note row x=13

findings.location: identity bar, first and last elements ('← aztec' x=25, 'Download trace' right edge x=1896)

findings.location: identity bar, scrubber between the stepping buttons and the 'Engine loading — 18 MB' status (x≈690-845, y≈8-24)

findings.location: Call Trace / Event Log tabbed region, the area below the 'Sorted by call order' footer (x 690-1145, y 370-582)
findings.finding: 212 px — 45% of the tabbed region's 471 px height — is empty black below the last call frame, while the Values pane directly beneath it packs ten rows flush to its bottom border with ~16 px of slack and the Code pane beside it clips every function signature mid-glyph at its right edge. findings.location: identity bar, full width of the top strip
findings.finding: Six distinct type treatments run across one 44px strip with no repeating pattern: sans link ("aztec"), bold mono hash, title-case amber pill ("Partial"), sans+mono compound ("block 101"), sans sentence status ("Engine loading - 18 MB"), mono ratio ("128 / 1315") and uppercase letterspaced phase chips. findings.location: Call Trace pane, rows 4 and 7 (`calculate_remaining_shie...`)

Two frames in a seven-frame fixture already hit this; a realistic forty-frame trace makes the deep rows mutually indistinguishable.

findings.location: Values pane, `masses` row
findings.finding: Every scalar value lands on one right edge (10000, 9000, 10, 200, 200, 90, 2000, 1000, 2) - a genuine tabular column. findings.location: Transaction pane COST · MANA row and identity bar position readout, versus Call Trace ACIR opcodes column

findings.location: Code pane, the two-line note between the file tab strip and line 26
findings.finding: "Showing from line 26 - the session's position is below, and the lines above it are not in this window." is the only sentence-shaped prose in the pane, set at label size across the pane's full measure, and it consumes two of the pane's rows to restate what the gutter's first number already says. It sits directly above a monospace listing and belongs to no other type level in the pane, so the pane opens on a paragraph rather than on code.

findings.location: Transaction pane, header block (truncated hash, then full hash immediately below)

Two different truncation lengths for one datum is a strategy that has not been decided; the full value directly under a truncation of itself also spends three lines of a 190px column on one fact.

findings.location: Transaction pane, FEE PAYER and TARGET value cells

findings.location: Call Trace pane, header row

Every other label on the page (CODE, VALUES, TRANSACTION, BLOCK, CANONICAL, FINALITY, SELECTOR, RAW) is uniformly uppercase; this is the one header cell that is not, and the unit carried alongside the acronym is what breaks it.

findings.location: Call Trace pane, current frame (row 6, `calculate_damage`)

findings.location: Code pane, right edge at lines 26, 40, 42, 48, 49, 53

findings.location: Call Trace / Event Log region, area below the 'Sorted by call order' footer (middle column, y 367-578)
findings.finding: The tabbed region is 467 px tall (y 111-578) but its content ends at y 367, leaving 211 px — 45% of the region — as blank pane. findings.location: top edge of the Call Trace / Event Log region versus the Code and Transaction panes

findings.location: identity bar, vertical space between row 1 (stepping/scrubber/phase rail) and row 2 (NOIR / Share / Download trace)
findings.finding: The bar wraps at laptop width between the phase rail and the language badge plus the two actions. findings.location: identity bar, row 2 right of 'Download trace' (x 340-1440) versus the scrubber on row 1 (x 687-846)
findings.finding: Row 2 uses only its leftmost 340 px and leaves ~1,100 px — 76% of the bar width — empty, while row 1 is packed edge to edge and the timeline, the element that most rewards width, gets 159 px for 1,315 steps. Width has been left unused on one row while being rationed on the other.

findings.location: Code pane, right border (x=685) — lines 26, 40, 48, 49 and 53
findings.finding: The pane gives roughly 66 columns after the line-number gutter, and five of the ~30 visible lines are cut hard at the pane border mid-identifier ('initial_shield, re', 'remaining_shi', 'as u') with no ellipsis and no visible horizontal scroll affordance, so nothing on screen says the line continues.

findings.location: Transaction pane, FEE PAYER and TARGET rows (x 1258-1427)
findings.finding: 42-character hashes are right-aligned into a ~170 px value column and wrap to three lines whose last line holds two characters ('32' for FEE PAYER, '4c' for TARGET). The ragged left edge plus the orphan fragment makes one value read as three, and the same treatment recurs down the pane.

findings.location: Call Trace, the two depth-4 'calculate_remaining_shie…' rows

findings.location: identity bar, left and right insets versus the pane grid below it
findings.finding: Bar content starts at x=26 and ends at x=1378, so the bar is inset 26 px left and 62 px right. The pane grid below is inset 6 px left and 4 px right. Neither the bar's two sides nor the bar and the grid share a vertical edge.

findings.location: Code pane header area — 'CODE' title, file-tab strip, and the 'Showing from line 26' note
findings.finding: Three stacked elements in one pane use two different left insets: the title and the note sit at x=14 (8 px from the border) while the file-tab strip starts at x=22 (16 px). The pane header has no single left edge.

findings.location: Transaction pane, BLOCK row, the '101:0' link

The block link and its underline extend to x=1434, 7 px past that edge and 2 px from the pane border, breaking the value column's right edge at exactly one row.

findings.location: Call Trace, frame-name indentation (x 702 / 724 / 739 / 755)
findings.finding: The first nesting step is 22 px and every deeper step is 15-16 px, because the depth-1 guide gutter is added once rather than per level; a single guide rule at x=706 serves depths 2 through 4. findings.location: pane grid — borders at x=4, x=686/691, x=1144/1149, x=1435; row separators in Call Trace and Values
findings.finding: The surface ladder is #101010 / #161616 / #1b1b1b / #202020, with adjacent steps at 1.051, 1.051 and 1.057:1 — no step is perceptible, so pane identity is carried entirely by dividers that are themselves below the 3:1 non-text floor: the pane border #3a3a3a is 1.51:1 over #1b1b1b and 1.67:1 over #101010, and the row separator #282828 is 1.13:1 over #1b1b1b. This is B4's named failure — panes distinguished only by a hairline — with the hairline too faint to distinguish them.

findings.location: Code pane body vs page canvas and pane headers (CODE at y=92-110 vs CALL TRACE / VALUES / TRANSACTION headers)
findings.finding: Surface levels are not assigned systematically. The Code pane body is #101010 — byte-identical to the page canvas (the 4px outer margin) and to the gutter between the Code and nav columns (x=687-690), so the pane has zero surface separation from the page. The other three pane bodies are #1b1b1b. Meanwhile the shared header token #161616 is lighter than the Code body but darker than the other three bodies, so the same header sits raised above its body in one pane and recessed below it in the other three. Elevation therefore has no consistent meaning.

findings.location: indigo #818cf8 across: back link '← aztec' (x=12,y=13), 'Sort by cost' (x=1099,y=357), '101:0' (x=1406,y=249), active tab underline (y=137-138 under CALL TRACE), active file tab underline (y=136-137 under src/shield.nr), scrubber played fill (x=687-701), Values changed rows (9000, 2000, and their left edge bars at x=692-694)
findings.finding: One token, #818cf8, carries five unrelated meanings: 'this is a link', 'this tab is open', 'this file is open', 'this much of the trace has played', and 'this value changed at step N'. A reader cannot tell from colour whether an indigo string in the Values pane is clickable or is a diff marker. §9 names a colour role used for two meanings as below bar; this is five.

findings.location: Values pane — rows 'remaining_shield 9000' (y=647) and 'damage 2000' (y=815) vs 'initial_shield 10000' (y=622), 'mass 200' (y=764), 'regeneration 1000' (y=840)
